title: सन्तान प्राप्तिको उपाय र वेदकालीन सांस्कृतिक परिवेश Santan Praptiko Upaya ra bedkalin Sanskritik Pariwesh
nepali: सन्तानको महत्व, उत्पादन एंव उत्पादन गर्ने पद्दती समाज व्यवस्थाको सामाजिक तथा सांस्कृतिक परिवेशले निर्माण गर्दछ । समाज व्यवस्थाको सामाजिक तथा सांस्कृतिक ऐतिहासिक जगमा निर्माण भएको हुन्छ । यसै सन्दर्भसँग जोडिएर यस आलेख भित्र प्राचीन परिवेशको परावर्तन दिने वेदकालीन सामाजिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संरचनामा सन्तान, सन्तानको महत्व र सन्तान उत्पादनका उपायहरूको खोजी गरिएको छ । यस उद्देश्य प्राप्तीका लागि सर्वप्राचीन ऐतिहासिक सांस्कृतिक ग्रन्थ वेद, वेदकालीन तथा प्राचीन भारतीय सामाजिक इतिहाससँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न सन्दर्भ ग्रन्थ, अनुसन्धानमूलक लेख लगायतका विभिन्न सन्र्दभहरूबाट  द्वितीय श्रोतको रूपमा प्राप्त भएका सूचनाहरूलाई ऐतिहासिक अन्तरवस्तु विश्लेषण विधिका माध्यमबाट विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययन कार्य वाट वेदकालीन समाजमा पशुधन एवं जमिनको बृहतीकरण अनिवार्य रहेको पाईयो । बृहतकिरणको प्रकृयाले आर्जित साधन स्रोतको संरक्षण र हस्तान्तरणकोलागि सन्तानको महत्व  रहने गरेको देखियो । त्यसका लागि सन्तानमध्ये पनि छोराको निकै महत्व र आवश्यकता मानेको पाईयो । अश्मारोहण, पाणीग्रहण लगायत विवाहका संस्कारजन्य विधिमा महिलाका खुट्टा पुज्ने, सम्मानका साथ सँगै जीवन जीउने बाचासहित हात समात्ने कार्य हुने गरेका तथ्यहरूले पितृसतात्मक ढाँचामा रहेको वेदकालीन समाजभित्र पनि छोरीरूको सम्मान र सहभागिता रहेको देखियो । त्यस समयमा छोरीहरूलाई पनि उचित सम्मान र आदर गर्ने गरेको तथ्यहरू प्रकाशमा आएका छन् ।
american_english: The importance of offspring, reproduction, and reproductive methods are constructed by the social and cultural environment of the social system. The social and cultural dimension of the social system is built on a historical foundation. Linked to this context, this article explores offspring, the importance of offspring, and methods of producing offspring within the Vedic social and cultural structure reflecting the ancient milieu. To achieve this objective, information obtained as secondary sources from the most ancient historical and cultural texts, the Vedas, and various reference works, research articles, and other materials related to Vedic and ancient Indian social history was analyzed using the historical content analysis method. From this research work, the expansion of livestock and land was found to be indispensable in Vedic society. Offspring were seen to hold importance for the preservation and transfer of resources and assets acquired through the process of expansion. For that purpose, among offspring, a son in particular was found to be considered of great importance and necessity. Facts such as worshiping women's feet and holding hands with vows to live life together with dignity during ritual marriage rites, including Ashmarohana and Panigrahana, showed that respect for and participation of daughters existed even within the patriarchal framework of Vedic society. Facts have come to light that during that era daughters were also accorded proper honor and respect.
british_english: The importance of offspring, reproduction and reproductive methods are constructed by the social and cultural environment of the social system. The social and cultural dimension of the social system is established upon a historical foundation. Linked with this context, this paper explores offspring, the importance of offspring and methods of producing offspring within the Vedic social and cultural structure reflecting the ancient setting. To attain this objective, information obtained as secondary sources from the most ancient historical-cultural texts, the Vedas, as well as various reference texts, research articles and other materials related to Vedic and ancient Indian social history was analysed using the method of historical content analysis. From this research work, the expansion of livestock and land was found to be imperative in Vedic society. Offspring were observed to hold importance for the preservation and transfer of resources acquired through the process of expansion. For that purpose, among offspring, a son was found to be regarded as of notable importance and necessity. Facts such as the veneration of women's feet and the holding of hands with pledges to live life together with dignity during sacramental marriage rites, including Ashmarohana and Panigrahana, demonstrated that respect for and participation of daughters was present even within the patriarchal framework of Vedic society. Facts have emerged that during that period daughters were also accorded due honour and respect.
